requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function, an altstep and a testcase ARE used to specify and structure test behaviour, define default behaviour and structure computation in a module.
requirements.original: In TTCN-3, functions, altsteps and testcases are used to specify and structure test behaviour, define default behaviour and to structure computation in a module, etc. as described in the following clauses.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function IS used to express test behaviour, to organize test execution or to structure computation in a module.
requirements.original: Functions are used in TTCN-3 to express test behaviour, to organize test execution or to structure computation in a module, for example, to calculate a single value, to initialize a set of variables or to check some condition.

requirements.subject: ent:function-definition
requirements.canonical: A function definition has the syntax `function` [`@deterministic` | `@control`] (FunctionIdentifier | `control`) "(" [{(FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar) [","]}] ")" [`runs on` ComponentType] [`mtc` ComponentType] [`system` ComponentType] [`return` [TemplateModifier] TypeOrNestedTypeDef [ArrayDef]] StatementBlock.
requirements.original:
function [ @deterministic | @control ] ( FunctionIdentifier | control )
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")"
  [ runs on ComponentType ] 
  [ mtc ComponentType ]
  [ system ComponentType ]
  [ return [ TemplateModifier ] TypeOrNestedTypeDef [ArrayDef] ]
  StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:function-definition
requirements.canonical: A function definition MAY carry at most one of the modifiers `@deterministic` and `@control`.
requirements.original:
function [ @deterministic | @control ] ( FunctionIdentifier | control )
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")"
  [ runs on ComponentType ] 
  [ mtc ComponentType ]
  [ system ComponentType ]
  [ return [ TemplateModifier ] TypeOrNestedTypeDef [ArrayDef] ]
  StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:function-definition
requirements.canonical: The `runs on`, `mtc`, `system` and `return` clauses of a function definition are optional and, when present, appear in this order before the statement block.
requirements.original:
function [ @deterministic | @control ] ( FunctionIdentifier | control )
  "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")"
  [ runs on ComponentType ] 
  [ mtc ComponentType ]
  [ system ComponentType ]
  [ return [ TemplateModifier ] TypeOrNestedTypeDef [ArrayDef] ]
  StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function IS a portion of TTCN-3 behaviour that performs a specific task and is relatively independent of the remaining behaviour.
requirements.original: Functions are portions of TTCN-3 behaviour, which perform a specific task and are relatively independent of the remaining behaviour.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function MAY return a value or a template.
requirements.original: Functions may return a value or a template.

requirements.subject: ent:return-clause
requirements.canonical: A value return IS denoted in the function header by the `return` keyword followed by a type expression.
requirements.original: Value return is denoted by the return keyword followed by a type expression.

requirements.subject: ent:return-clause
requirements.canonical: A template return IS denoted in the function header by the `return` keyword followed by a TemplateModifier and a type expression.
requirements.original: Template return is denoted by the return keywords followed by a TemplateModifier and a type expression.

ambiguity.issue: The plural 'return keywords' is used although only the single `return` keyword is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: Execution of a return statement in the body of a function evaluates the return value or template.
requirements.original: Execution of a return statement in the body of the function causes evaluation of the return value or template, the function to terminate and to return the result to the location of the call of the function.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: Execution of a return statement in the body of a function terminates the function.
requirements.original: Execution of a return statement in the body of the function causes evaluation of the return value or template, the function to terminate and to return the result to the location of the call of the function.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: Execution of a return statement in the body of a function returns the result to the location of the call of the function.
requirements.original: Execution of a return statement in the body of the function causes evaluation of the return value or template, the function to terminate and to return the result to the location of the call of the function.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: The behaviour of a function CAN be defined by using the statements and operations described in clauses 18 to 26.
requirements.original: The behaviour of a function can be defined by using statements and operations described in clauses 18 to 26.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function MAY be parameterized.
requirements.original: Functions may be parameterized.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function MAY have an mtc clause.
requirements.original: Functions may have an mtc clause.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc-clause
requirements.condition: the function has an mtc clause
requirements.canonical: If a function has an mtc clause, the component type referenced by the mtc clause SHALL be mtc-compatible with the type of the mtc component reference.
requirements.original: If a function has an mtc clause, the type referenced by this clause shall be mtccompatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the mtc component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:mtc-component-reference
requirements.condition: the mtc clause is not present
requirements.canonical: If a function has no mtc clause, the type of the mtc component reference IS unknown in the scope of the function.
requirements.original: If the mtc clause is not present, the type of the mtc component reference is unknown in the scope of this function.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function MAY have a system clause.
requirements.original: Functions may have a system clause.

requirements.subject: ent:system-clause
requirements.condition: the function has a system clause
requirements.canonical: If a function has a system clause, the component type referenced by the system clause SHALL be system-compatible with the type of the system component reference.
requirements.original: If a function has a system clause, the type referenced by this clause shall be system-compatible (see clause 6.3.2.7) with the type of the system component reference.

requirements.subject: ent:system-component-reference
requirements.condition: the system clause is not present
requirements.canonical: If a function has no system clause, the type of the system component reference IS unknown in the scope of the function.
requirements.original: If the system clause is not present, the type of the system component reference is unknown in the scope of this function.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-modifier
requirements.canonical: A function MAY be declared deterministic by using the `@deterministic` modifier.
requirements.original: Using the @deterministic modifier, a function can be declared to be deterministic.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-function
requirements.canonical: A deterministic function IS safe to be called from specific places where non-determinism could lead to unexpected side effects.
requirements.original: Deterministic functions are safe to be used when called from specific places where non-determinism could lead to unexpected side effects (see clause 16.1.4).

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-function
requirements.canonical: The determinism of a function marked `@deterministic` IS NOT required to be exhaustively checked by a tool, as the determination of determinism is semi-decidable.
requirements.original: NOTE 0: The determination of determinism of a function is a semi-decidable problem and as such can and will not be exhaustively checked.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-modifier
requirements.canonical: The `@deterministic` annotation IS mainly used for informational purposes and for allowing certain functions to be used during snapshot evaluation.
requirements.original: As such, the annotation deterministic is mainly used for informational purposes and for allowing certain functions to be used during snapshot evaluation.

requirements.subject: ent:deterministic-function
requirements.canonical: A function CAN be seen as deterministic if it does not violate any of the restrictions of clause 16.1.4; a violation of these restrictions does not automatically imply non-determinism.
requirements.original: Principally, a function can be seen as deterministic if it does not violate any of the restrictions from clause 16.1.4 which does not mean that violation of these restriction automatically leads to non-determinism.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function has no runs on clause
requirements.canonical: A function without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT locally invoke a function that has a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: a) A function without runs on clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a runs on clause locally.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function has no runs on clause
requirements.canonical: A function without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT locally invoke an altstep that has a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: a) A function without runs on clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a runs on clause locally.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function has no runs on clause
requirements.canonical: A function without a `runs on` clause SHALL NOT activate as default an altstep that has a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: a) A function without runs on clause shall never invoke a function or altstep or activate an altstep as default with a runs on clause locally.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function is started with the start test component operation
requirements.canonical: A function started by the start test component operation SHALL have a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: b) Functions started by using the start test component operation shall always have a runs on clause (see clause 22.5) and are considered to be invoked in the component to be started, i.e. not locally.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function started by the start test component operation IS considered to be invoked in the component to be started, not locally.
requirements.original: b) Functions started by using the start test component operation shall always have a runs on clause (see clause 22.5) and are considered to be invoked in the component to be started, i.e. not locally.

requirements.subject: ent:start-component-operation
requirements.canonical: The start test component operation MAY be invoked within behaviour without a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: However, the start test component operation may be invoked within behaviour without a runs `on clause.`

requirements.subject: ent:runs-on-clause
requirements.canonical: The restrictions concerning the `runs on` clause in clause 16.1.0 apply only to functions and altsteps and not to testcases.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: The restrictions concerning the runs `on clause are only related to functions and altsteps and not to test` cases.

ambiguity.issue: 'test cases' is used for the TTCN-3 language element 'testcase'.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function is called directly or indirectly from a module control function
requirements.canonical: A function called directly or indirectly from a module control function SHALL NOT have an mtc clause or a system clause.
requirements.original: c) Functions called directly or indirectly from a module control function shall have no mtc or system clause.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function called directly or indirectly from the module control function MAY execute testcases.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: Nevertheless, functions called directly or indirectly from the module control function are allowed to execute test cases.

ambiguity.issue: 'test cases' is used for the TTCN-3 language element 'testcase'.

requirements.subject: ent:formal-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: The formal parameter list of a function SHALL follow the rules for formal parameter lists defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: d) The rules for formal parameter lists shall be followed as defined in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:return-clause
requirements.canonical: A return clause with a TemplateModifier SHALL obey the restrictions specified in clause 15.0.
requirements.original: e) For return TemplateModifier statements the restrictions specified in clause 15.0 shall apply.

improper_terms.proper: return clause with a template modifier

ambiguity.issue: The text speaks of 'statements', but the return TemplateModifier construct is part of the function header return clause, not a statement.

requirements.subject: ent:return-clause
requirements.canonical: A template return clause MAY be restricted to the matching mechanisms specific value and `omit` by a template restriction.
requirements.original: f) Template return can be restricted to the matching mechanisms specific value and omit, see clause 5.4.1.2.

readings: A template return clause MAY use the template restrictions `omit` and `value` (and `present`) as defined in clause 5.4.1.2.
A template return clause MAY only be restricted so that it permits specific values and `omit`, i.e. only the `omit` restriction.
ambiguity.issue: Clause 5.4.1.2 defines the restrictions omit, value and present; the sentence mentions only specific value and omit. The first reading (template restrictions per 5.4.1.2) is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: A return statement in a value returning function SHALL have a value expression compatible with the type specified in the return clause of the function header.
requirements.original: g) A return statement in a value returning function shall always have a value expression compatible to the type specified in the function header return clause.

requirements.subject: ent:return-statement
requirements.canonical: A return statement in a template returning function SHALL have a template reference (including a call of a value or template returning function) or a template instance compatible with the type specified in the return clause of the function header.
requirements.original: h) A return statement in a template returning function shall always have a template reference (including calling a value or template returning function)or template instance compatible to the type specified in the function header return clause.

requirements.subject: ent:template
requirements.condition: the return clause has a template restriction
requirements.canonical: If the return clause of a template returning function has a template restriction, the returned template SHALL adhere to that template restriction.
requirements.original: If the return clause has a template restriction, this restriction shall be adhered to by the returned template.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function header includes a return clause
requirements.canonical: If the function header includes a return clause, the function SHALL terminate by executing a return statement.
requirements.original: i) If the function header includes a return clause, the function, when terminating, shall do so by executing a return statement.

requirements.subject: ent:test-case-error
requirements.condition: the function has a return clause and reaches the end of its body without executing a return statement
requirements.canonical: If a function with a return clause reaches the end of its function body without executing a return statement, a test case error IS caused.
requirements.original: The function will cause a test case error if it terminates (i.e. reaches the end of the function body) without executing a return statement.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.condition: the function references definitions of a component type
requirements.canonical: If a function references names of definitions defined inside a component type definition, the function header SHALL reference that component type in a `runs on` clause.
requirements.original: j) If a function references the names of definitions that are defined inside a component type definition, the component type shall be referenced using the runs `on keywords in the function header.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function MAY omit the `runs on` clause if all the necessary component-wide information is passed to the function as parameters.
requirements.original: The one exception to` this rule is if all the necessary component-wide information is passed in the function as parameters.

readings: A function MAY omit the `runs on` clause when all component-wide information is passed as parameters, in which case it does not reference component definitions by name.
A function without `runs on` clause MAY reference component-type definitions by name if they are also passed as parameters.
ambiguity.issue: Contradictory phrasing: if the information is passed as parameters, the function references the parameters, not the component definitions. The first reading is chosen as the only consistent one.

requirements.subject: ent:control-function
requirements.canonical: An explicit control function SHALL obey the additional restrictions of clause 16.1.5.
requirements.original: k) The additional restrictions in clause 16.1.5 shall apply to all explicit control functions.

ambiguity.issue: 'explicit control function' is not defined elsewhere; presumably functions declared with the @control modifier are meant.

requirements.subject: ent:control-function
requirements.canonical: Table 15 lists the statements and operations that a control function is allowed to use.
requirements.original: The list of statements and operations that are allowed to be used by control functions is provided by table 15.

readings: Table 15 (as numbered in the text) lists the statements and operations allowed in control functions.
The referenced table is the one in clause 16.1.5 (not table 15, which in clause 16.1.2 lists predefined functions).
ambiguity.issue: Table 15 is the list of predefined functions in clause 16.1.2; the reference most likely means the table of clause 16.1.5. The second reading is assumed in cross_refs.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: Invoking a function with mtc and system clauses from a function lacking a mtc or system clause CAN cause a runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: A function with mtc and system clauses MAY invoke a function without mtc and system clauses.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: A function IS invoked by referring to its name and providing the list of actual parameters.
requirements.original: A function is invoked by referring to its name and providing the actual list of parameters.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: A function invocation has the syntax FunctionRef "(" [{ActualPar [","]}] ")".
requirements.original: FunctionRef "(" [ { ActualPar [","] } ] ")"

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: A function invocation results in the execution of the statement block of the invoked function.
requirements.original: A function invocation results in the execution of the statement block of the invoked function.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: The invoked function IS performed by the test component invoking it.
requirements.original: The invoked function is performed by the test component invoking it.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter
requirements.canonical: The actual parameters of a function invocation ARE passed into the statement block of the invoked function.
requirements.original: Actual parameters are passed into the statement block.

requirements.subject: ent:test-component
requirements.canonical: When the invoked function returns, the invoking test component continues its behaviour right after the function invocation.
requirements.original: If the function returns (upon termination and potentially with a return value), the test components continues its behaviour right after the function invocation.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.condition: the function does not return a value
requirements.canonical: A function that does not return a value SHALL be invoked directly (as a stand-alone statement).
requirements.original: a) Functions that do not return values shall be invoked directly.

readings: A function without return clause SHALL only be invoked as a stand-alone statement, not inside an expression.
A function that returns neither a value nor a template SHALL be invoked directly; template returning functions may appear in template expressions.
ambiguity.issue: 'do not return values' does not state how template returning functions are treated. The first reading (no return clause) is chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: A function that returns a value MAY be invoked directly or inside an expression.
requirements.original: Functions that return values may be invoked directly or inside expressions.

requirements.subject: ent:actual-parameter-list
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter list of a function invocation SHALL follow the rules for actual parameter lists defined in clause 5.4.
requirements.original: b) The rules for actual parameter lists shall be followed as defined in clause 5.4.

requirements.subject: ent:function
requirements.canonical: A function bound to a test component by the start test component operation SHALL obey the special restrictions described in clause 21.3.2.
requirements.original: c) Special restrictions apply to functions bound to test components using the start test component operation. These restrictions are described in clause 21.3.2.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: When a function is invoked, the test component type of the invoking test component SHALL be compatible with the `runs on` clause of the invoked function as described in clause 6.3.2.7.
requirements.original: d) When invoking a function, the compatibility to the test component type of the invoking test component as described in clause 6.3.2.7 need to be fulfilled.

ambiguity.issue: Non-standard modal 'need to' is used instead of 'shall'; also the object of the compatibility (the runs on clause of the invoked function) is implicit.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: When a function is invoked, the mtc and system clauses of the invoked function SHALL be mtc- and system-compatible with the actual mtc and system types of the running test case as described in clause 6.3.2.7.
requirements.original: f) When invoking a function, the mtc and system compatibility of the mtc and system components of the invoked function with the actual mtc and system types of the running test case as described in clause 6.3.2.7 need to be fulfilled.

improper_terms.used: mtc and system components of the invoked function
improper_terms.proper: mtc and system clauses of the invoked function

ambiguity.issue: Non-standard modal 'need to'; 'mtc and system components' refers to the component types of the mtc and system clauses.

requirements.subject: ent:function-invocation
requirements.canonical: A function that returns an uninitialized value MAY be invoked only directly as a statement of a statement block or as the return value of a return statement.
requirements.original: g) Invoking a function that returns an uninitialized value is allowed only if the function is invoked directly as a statement of a statement block or as the return value of a return statement.

requirements.subject: ent:error
requirements.condition: the function returns an uninitialized value
requirements.canonical: Invoking a function that returns an uninitialized value in any other place than as a statement or as the value of a return statement (e.g. in an expression, as an actual parameter or on the right hand side of an assignment) SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: In any other place, invoking a function that returns an uninitialized value shall cause an error (e.g. in an expression, as an actual parameter or on the right hand side of an assignment).

readings: The invocation SHALL cause a runtime error (dynamic test case error) when the returned value is actually uninitialized.
A tool SHALL reject the invocation at compile time if the function may return an uninitialized value.
ambiguity.issue: It is not stated whether the error is a compile-time or runtime error; the runtime reading is chosen since uninitializedness is in general only known at runtime.

non_requirement.reason: introductory sentence of the restrictions list; restrictions extracted from items a)..k)
introductory sentence of the restrictions list; restrictions extracted from items a)..g)
pointer to clause 21.3.2; included in TTCN3-CORE-16.1.1-011a
